name: token-bench
desc: Free, open-source tokens-per-second benchmark for local LLMs on Windows — quant and thread sweeps with charts. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Automated sweeps** — run every quant of a model back to back and rank them by generation speed
✅ **Split metrics** — prompt processing and token generation timed separately, like llama-bench does
✅ **Thread and offload grid** — finds the thread count and GPU layer sweet spot instead of guessing
✅ **Chart view** — bars and sparklines per run, printable report for comparing two machines
✅ **Warmup control** — configurable warmup rounds so cache effects do not poison the first result
✅ **CSV export** — every run lands in a spreadsheet-ready file with model, quant and settings columns
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and benchmark backend bundled, portable, offline, MIT
compare: | Feature | **token-bench** | llama-bench CLI | LM Studio | KoboldCpp |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Free | Free, OSS |
| GUI sweep across quants | **Yes** | Scripted | No | No |
| Thread and offload grid | **Yes** | Flags | No | Partial |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Build needed | Installer | Zip |
faqQ: how to benchmark LLM tokens per second on Windows?
faqA: Command-line benchmarks work but reading flags and collating numbers across quants is a chore. token-bench runs the sweep for you, separates prompt processing from generation and turns results into charts and CSV. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, and results stay on your machine.
s1: Dark bench view (#121417, blue #60A5FA): run table with quant, threads, tok per sec columns, selected row charted above with generation and prompt bars.
s2: Sweep setup wizard: model list with five quants checked, thread range 4 to 16, warmup rounds stepper at 2, estimated time chip reading 38 minutes.
s3: Report page: two-machine comparison chart, best-config summary card, export CSV button, log tail showing run 14 of 20 complete.
